Just to clarify, a bug out bag is basically a kit to travel out of a disaster area. So keep that in mind. Stay-put survival gear will be different.

First of all, WAY more flashlights and or headlamps. They're cheap and essential so have several for each of you, plus several spare sets of batteries.

Get a second backpack for your fiance, and make sure she's got a pair of boots she can hike all day in.

I'd throw in basic protection for various disaster scenarios, for example a pack of potassium iodide pills (the high dose rad protection ones). For disease type threats: surgical masks, nitrile gloves, hand sanitizer, and maybe a couple disposable tyvec suites (I see that you already have most of that). Obviously you would ditch the stuff that's not relevant before heading out.

Second the hand ratchet (for travel by car), plus chains if you're in the north, and maybe a couple of gas cans. You will have to periodically use and refill the gas cans to keep them fresh.

I'd add anti-diahrrhea meds your first aid kit.

Add some barter goods, such as a carton of cigarettes, cash, etc.

Consider a second handgun for your fiance. Even if she only practices with it once a year, just having it will provide protection. You might need to leave her somewhere and go get supplies or whatever.

Ditch the glow sticks, and hand crank radio. Those aren't essential and add weight. Those crank radios are trash anyway.

Figure out charging/power solutions for your electronics in the field. At least 12v and wall chargers for your important devices. Plus aligator clips so you can steal power from various things in the environment like car batteries.

Duct Tape.

A cheap Chinese dual band radio would be useful, even if you don't have a license to actually use it.

Maybe 1 regular non-mylar blaket. Useful for more than just keeping warm.

An extra pair of glasses for each of you if you need them. You can get perfectly good glasses for like 20 bucks a pair from china so there's no excuse not to have backups.
